criterion: The console overview sits on a true near-black ground that runs edge to edge behind every panel.
evaluation_rule: Look at the area around the counters on the first screen after signing in. Yes if the ground behind them is black or all but black, with no lighter page colour showing at the edges. No if the ground is a mid grey or a white surface.

criterion: Bands on the emails log are separated by a hairline that fades to nothing at both ends.
evaluation_rule: A hairline here is a one pixel rule between two bands of content. Yes if the divider is brightest in the middle and disappears towards the left edge and the right edge. No if the divider is a solid line of even strength across the full width.

criterion: Pointing at the primary action on the credentials route makes the control appear to emit light.
evaluation_rule: Yes if hovering the main button surrounds the control with a soft outward white glow. No if hovering only darkens the fill or drops a dark shadow beneath the control.

criterion: A panel on the credentials route arrives by sliding a few pixels into a fade.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a panel appearing moves a very short distance, on the order of a few pixels, with an eased curve. No if a panel appears instantly at its final position or leaps in from off screen.

criterion: Body text on the emails log meets the WCAG AA contrast bar against its ground.
evaluation_rule: Yes if ordinary row text is comfortable to read at normal size against the dark ground, clearing a four and a half to one ratio. No if the row text is a dim grey that fades into the background.

criterion: At a narrow viewport the console left rail collapses to an icon strip.
evaluation_rule: Narrow here means a handset width, around 390 points across. Yes if the rail becomes a column of icons or a slide-over at that width. No if the full width rail stays in place or the page scrolls sideways.

criterion: Interface text across the console is set in Inter.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the computed font family on body text and table cells names Inter first. No if the text renders in a system default such as Helvetica, Arial or Segoe UI.

criterion: Message identifiers on the emails log are set in a monospace face with figures that align in a column.
evaluation_rule: Yes if identifier text is fixed width and the digits of stacked rows line up vertically. No if identifiers render in the same proportional face as the surrounding prose.

criterion: Each state chip on the emails log carries its state word beside its colour.
evaluation_rule: The states are queued, delivered, bounced, complained and canceled. Yes if every chip shows one of those words as text. No if a chip shows only a coloured dot or a bare glyph.

criterion: A tag chip on a message draws its colour from a fixed set of hues.
evaluation_rule: Yes if tag colours across several messages repeat from a small palette such as teal, orange, plum or lime. No if a person can pick an arbitrary colour from a full colour picker.

criterion: The primary action on the domains route reads as distinct from every secondary control on that route.
evaluation_rule: Yes if one control is filled or emphasised more strongly than the others, so a first-time visitor can say which to press. No if two or more controls look equally emphasised.

criterion: The console left rail groups its sending destinations above its marketing destinations.
evaluation_rule: Sending destinations are the overview, the emails log, domains, credentials and notifications. Marketing destinations are audiences and broadcasts. Yes if the first group sits above the second with a divider between. No if the destinations are in one undivided list.

criterion: The console usage route offers a plan name beside an allowance rather than a card entry form.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the usage screen shows a plan name beside a monthly allowance only. No if the screen asks for a card number, an expiry date or a billing address.

criterion: The credentials route shows a worked code sample that hands a message to the sending interface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the screen after a credential is minted carries a copyable example call naming a from address, a to address and a subject. No if the screen offers the secret with nothing showing how to use one.

criterion: The delivery chart on the overview states the instant its figures were computed.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a line beside or beneath the chart names a time such as computed at 09:15 UTC. No if the chart shows figures with nothing saying when they were worked out.
